conventions: Byte strings are lowercase hex. Codes, links, URLs, names, digit codes and JSON text are plain strings; decoded payloads are JSON objects.
Times are milliseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC.
Every secret and nonce here comes from SHA-256("kinfold-test-vector/" || tag); never reuse them outside tests.

hpke_rfc9180.source: RFC 9180 test vectors (github.com/cfrg/draft-irtf-cfrg-hpke, test-vectors.json): mode 0, KEM 0x0020, KDF 0x0001, AEAD 0x0002; first 2 of 257 encryptions

signatures.name: ordinary
signatures.description: a signature as RFC 8032 makes it

signatures.name: s_not_reduced
signatures.description: the same signature with L added to S (check 1)

signatures.name: small_order_key_0
signatures.description: the key is a point of order 1 (check 3)

signatures.name: small_order_key_1
signatures.description: the key is a point of order 8 (check 3)

signatures.name: small_order_key_2
signatures.description: the key is a point of order 4 (check 3)

signatures.name: small_order_key_3
signatures.description: the key is a point of order 8 (check 3)

signatures.name: small_order_key_4
signatures.description: the key is a point of order 2 (check 3)

signatures.name: small_order_key_5
signatures.description: the key is a point of order 8 (check 3)

signatures.name: small_order_key_6
signatures.description: the key is a point of order 4 (check 3)

signatures.name: small_order_key_7
signatures.description: the key is a point of order 8 (check 3)

signatures.name: noncanonical_key_0
signatures.description: the key is written as y = 1 with the sign bit set (checks 2 and 3)

signatures.name: noncanonical_key_1
signatures.description: the key is written as y = p - 1 with the sign bit set (checks 2 and 3)

signatures.name: noncanonical_key_2
signatures.description: the key is written as y = p (checks 2 and 3)

signatures.name: noncanonical_key_3
signatures.description: the key is written as y = p with the sign bit set (checks 2 and 3)

signatures.name: noncanonical_key_4
signatures.description: the key is written as y = p + 1 (checks 2 and 3)

signatures.name: noncanonical_key_5
signatures.description: the key is written as y = p + 1 with the sign bit set (checks 2 and 3)

signatures.name: small_order_r_identity
signatures.description: R is the identity and S = k*a (check 3)

signatures.name: noncanonical_r
signatures.description: R is the identity written as y = p + 1 (check 2)

signatures.name: small_order_r_1
signatures.description: R is a point of order 8; the key's torsion part cancels it (check 3)

signatures.name: small_order_r_4
signatures.description: R is a point of order 2; the key's torsion part cancels it (check 3)

signatures.name: mixed_key_torsion_cancels
signatures.description: key = [a]B + (a point of order 2); k mod L is even, so the torsion part drops out

signatures.name: mixed_key_torsion_remains
signatures.description: the same key; k mod L is odd. A verifier that multiplies by the cofactor would accept this

signatures.name: mixed_key_k_reduced_first
signatures.description: the same key; k mod L is even but the unreduced 512-bit k is odd. Accepting it shows k is reduced before it multiplies the key

signatures.name: mixed_key_k_reduced_first_reject
signatures.description: the same key; k mod L is odd but the unreduced k is even

signatures.name: mixed_key_order_8_cancels
signatures.description: key = [a]B + (a point of order 8); k mod L is a multiple of 8

signatures.name: mixed_key_order_8_remains
signatures.description: the same key; k mod L is 4 mod 8

signatures.name: mixed_key_and_r
signatures.description: R and the key both carry the point of order 2, and k mod L is odd, so the two cancel

signatures.name: key_not_on_curve
signatures.description: the key's y is on no curve point: it passes the byte checks, and nothing verifies under it

keys.note: mixed order: not caught by the byte checks, and allowed
not on the curve: no separate check (3.3)
an ordinary key with the top bit set
